items.title: Identity-keyed byte cache in front of resolution: an in-process range broker that mpv reads through stream_cb
items.change: Add an AudioBroker on its own thread. mpv reads it through a registered monolist:// protocol (mpv_stream_cb_add_ro). It serves each rendition from a disk store keyed yt:<videoId>:<itag>:<clen>, later saavn:<id>:<kbps>. It pins the rendition an identity last played (C4), so beginTrack can play a complete entry without resolving at all. On a miss it fills the entry write-through from the resolver's URL; the first upstream read doubles as the probe (C11), and a mid-file 403 is re-resolved and continued at the same byte offset once itag, clen and lmt are checked. Video, local files, downloads and manifests keep today's direct path, and a settings kill-switch restores direct googlevideo URLs, so the YouTube ladder underneath is untouched.

First play after launch of a cached song: 677 ms, or 1,048 at window-ready -> ~150 ms, with no /player call and no visitorData wait. Network per replay: 3-6 MB -> 0 (today 178 opens fetched 178 files). First play of a new song: unchanged at ~553.5 ms and must not regress by more than ~10 ms.
items.risk: stream_cb.h marks the API 'not stable yet' and forbids calling libmpv from its callbacks (deadlock). A blocking read_fn that never returns would freeze mpv's demuxer, so every wait needs cancel_fn plus a ~20 s stall timeout that returns -1, which lets the existing loadFailed ladder run. Two different files spliced into one entry (the §5.4 corruption): refill only when itag+clen+lmt match, otherwise start a new key. Disk full or locked files on Windows: play through uncached, and never fail playback because of the cache. The store is listening history on disk: cap it (1 GiB default, whole-entry LRU with the current and next entries pinned), give it a Clear action, and honour MONOLIST_DATA_DIR for tests. The work touches the same functions as the jiosaavn branch (handleResolved, the loadFailed handler, StreamResolver::succeed), so build it after that merge. Fallback design if stream_cb misbehaves: the same store served by a 127.0.0.1 HTTP server that mpv reads with its own curl. It must use a random port and a per-session token in the path, and serve identity URLs only, never act as an open proxy.

Cases: byte-exact assembly (md5 against the source); a seek into an unfilled span; a 403 after the first request (must continue with no mpv error); a different clen on refresh (must error, never splice); a truncated body (must error, never EOF); cancel during a blocked read. Real tracks: re-apply scratchpad bench/instrumentation.diff and run bench/bench_B.ps1. The 'again' suite must show a TTFA-warm median < 200 ms with 0 network bytes logged, and the 'seq' cold median must stay within ±10 ms of 553.5. Two launches of --play <id> 30 prove cross-launch hits, and the kill-switch must reproduce today's numbers.

S3 (headers kept apart from the cached URL: store them in the entry). S4 (a cache not keyed by quality: key by rendition). §5.2's silent end after MAX_EMPTY_RANGES (a short or refused range is an error, never EOF). §5.4's 8 s cache-lock stalls (one fill task per key shared by all readers; no second writer).

items.title: Next-track and launch-track byte prefetch into the broker
items.change: Fill the next queue row's rendition once the current entry's fill completes (a typical song is whole ~0.75 s after it starts) or 3 s after start, whichever comes first: the whole file if it is ≤ 16 MiB, otherwise the first 4 MiB. Fetch only the link for the row after that, and at launch fill the paused track the app opens on. Prefetch the rendition that would actually play (JioSaavn's when the jiosaavn branch's verdict is a Match and JioSaavn is on), fetch links only on a metered connection (QNetworkInformation), and re-target through the existing prefetchUpcoming calls.

items.risk: Competition with the current track's start: begin only after its fill completes. Bandwidth spent on songs that are skipped over: log a wasted-bytes counter, and fetch links only when metered. A prefetched URL that is later refused must never fail playback: that play simply fills from the network as a miss. Shuffle and repeat changes leave stale fills: cancel on re-target, but let a fill that is more than half done finish (§11 row 8). Coordinate with any §8 gapless plan that moves to mpv's own playlist (loadfile append + prefetch-playlist), so that only one side schedules prefetch. mpv would then open the next monolist:// entry early, and the byte cache still serves it.

D7 (a fixed 8 s delay: start when the current fill completes instead). §5.4's 64 KiB lock-probe waste (there is never a second writer, so no probe is needed).

items.title: One shared, persisted visitorData (supersedes ROADMAP G06; raise it from P8)
items.change: Move visitorData out of the six InnerTube objects into one process-wide holder that only the stream side fetches. Persist the value and its fetch time in the settings table, so a launch uses it at once, and refresh it in the background after the first play. When /player answers LOGIN_REQUIRED while a stored id is in use, refresh once and retry /player before falling to yt-dlp. The other five objects keep only their TLS pre-open. Measure www.youtube.com/sw.js_data (§3.2.6) as a smaller refresh source than the 885 KB home page, and leave the holder able to take a session-bound id from the pending sign-in work, which outranks the anonymous one.

items.title: Close the recovery-ladder gaps: truncated streams, refused local files, the failure counter (C32)
items.change: On a stream, treat an end of file that arrives well before the known duration (position < duration - max(5 s, 3%)) as a failure: re-resolve the same rendition once and resume at the position, instead of advancing. When mpv refuses a downloaded or local file, stream the song (or skip it) instead of halting. Reset the three-in-a-row failure counter only when audio actually starts, not when a resolve succeeds.

items.title: Bound the resolve: an overall deadline, one hedged /player, a non-blocking yt-dlp cancel (C8)
items.change: Give a foreground resolve an overall deadline of 20 s. Give /player a total (not idle) deadline of ~3 s, with one hedged second /player on a fresh connection if nothing has arrived at ~1.2 s. Start the yt-dlp tier at ~3 s instead of after 8 s + 1.2 s + 8 s. Log InnerTube's failure reason and elapsed time, and make cancelling a resolve-only yt-dlp request non-blocking (today it can wait up to 2 s + 1 s on the UI thread).

A deadline that is too tight on a slow network would fail tracks that would have played: keep the numbers as constants and log them. Add a second no-cipher client (e.g. the paper's ANDROID_VR or visionOS 0.1 entries) only if the new log shows InnerTube failing with LOGIN_REQUIRED or with no plain URL. The yt-dlp cancel fix can land before the jiosaavn merge; the rest touches the resolver after it.

items.title: Range-chunk only long files, inside the broker, with a transparent mid-file refresh (C5)
items.change: In the broker's upstream fetch, keep a single request while the span still to fetch is ≤ 8 MiB (today's fast path); above that, read sequential 4 MiB Range requests on the kept-alive connection. On a mid-file 403, 404 or 410, re-resolve the same rendition and continue at the byte offset; reopen a short read at most 3 times, then fail loudly. Send JioSaavn's CDN a single request until its pacing has been measured.
items.files: src/audiobroker.* (upstream policy, range-size constants, refresh); src/streamresolver.* (a 'refresh this rendition' call that returns the same itag or fails); interim only: src/mpvengine.cpp:343-398 (set curl-max-request-size per file only when the URL's clen > 8 MiB, as the ytdl_hook embedded in libmpv-2.dll sets file-local-options/curl-max-request-size).
items.metric: Download rate for files > 8 MiB (1 of 12 benchmark tracks; roughly 9-10 min or more of 155 kbps Opus): 36.8 kB/s in the app (14.6 MB in 396.7 s, 9 plays) -> ~4-8 MB/s. On the same URLs with curl, 1 MiB ranges ran at a median 4.3-6.8 MB/s, and single 4-8 MiB ranges at 3.9-11.3 MB/s. Buffer ahead after 1 s of play: 2.1 s -> the whole file within ~2-4 s. Audible today: nothing (0 stalls in 1,555 s of continuous play). The gain is headroom (the paced 36 kB/s is only 1.1x a 256 kbps rendition from the sign-in slot), fast seeks deep into long tracks, and long tracks that can be cached and prefetched.
items.risk: The 'first request served, every later one 403' mode (2 of 8 fresh long-track URLs with curl) would hit every chunked long track that draws such a URL. Without the broker's refresh (that is, with the mpv-option interim) it becomes a mid-song error or a silent EOF, so the interim needs PP-06 first. The 8-12 MiB pacing threshold comes from one track on one evening: keep the sizes as constants, log per-request rates, and re-measure on 3 or more long tracks. Chunking small files would slow them down (1 MiB ranges 0.9-5.7 MB/s against 6.0 MB/s for one GET), hence the threshold.

On the fake server, a 403 after the first range must cause no mpv error, and the entry's md5 must equal a whole-file curl download. items.title: Resolver cache hygiene: join duplicate resolves, keep cancelled answers, add a negative cache and a bounded link cache (C12)
items.change: Make resolve() and resolveVia() join a running foreground job for the same id instead of cancelling and restarting it. Let an in-flight /player answer that arrives after its job was cancelled still fill the link cache. Add a 10-minute 'unplayable' verdict per videoId, written only when every tier failed for non-network reasons, so prefetch finds it early and the transition skips at once. Bound the link cache to ~256 entries (LRU), and give links that have not yet served bytes a 20-minute TTL.

items.title: Downloads reuse a complete cache entry (C34)
items.change: Before starting yt-dlp for a download, ask the broker for a complete entry of the rendition the chosen format needs (Opus 251 for 'original', AAC 140 for m4a). rejected: A separate probe request before caching a URL (C11 as BitChord does it; D6). A probe is one extra request on a new connection, ~200 ms (HTTP open median 200.5 ms), on every cold play: +36% on the 553.5 ms cold TTFA. It would catch refusals on 1.1% of opens (2 of 178), all of them on the first request, which PP-01's first real read detects at no cost. The mid-file 'one request, then 403' mode is handled by PP-08's refresh, which a probe at 1 MiB could only partly predict.

1 MiB range chunking for every googlevideo read (§5.2 and §11 row 1 as written). Normal songs (≤ ~8 MiB) arrived whole at a median 6.0 MB/s in one request (n=93). On those files 1 MiB ranges were slower (0.9-5.7 MB/s, one TTFB per range). Every extra request also exposes the 'first request served, then 403' mode (2 of 8 fresh long-track URLs). PP-08 chunks only above 8 MiB.

mpv options alone as the byte cache (cache-on-disk, demuxer-cache-dir, dump-cache, stream-record). mpv's disk cache is a per-file temporary spill discarded at close, and dump-cache/stream-record remux packets, so the result is not byte-exact. None of them is keyed by identity, so replays, prefetch to disk (C17) and download reuse (C34) cannot come from them. mpv's per-file curl-max-request-size is kept only as a stop-gap for long tracks (the PP-08 interim).

Sending the minting client's User-Agent or per-client media headers, or unifying IPv4/IPv6 between mint and fetch, as a speed or 403 fix (§3.2.6, §11 row 10). The UA had no measurable effect: pacing was identical, and no 403 depended on the UA across the Chrome, visionOS, no-UA and mpv-exact variants (5 URLs x 8 variants). The IP family was not measured, and nothing points to a problem. The muxed tier keeps sending yt-dlp's headers as it does today.

Changing the start threshold or the buffer sizes (C19, C20, §5.6, §11 row 5). The time from the first response bytes to audio start is already a median 49 ms (p90 209, max 481, n=176) with mpv's defaults (cache-pause-initial=no), faster than a 500 ms threshold would be. There were 0 stalls in 2,319.7 audible seconds, and 64 MiB holds ~55 min of Opus. The only change worth making is cleanup: demuxer-readahead-secs=20 (src/mpvengine.cpp:152) is dead config.

Racing two InnerTube clients on every play (D3's 'race the top 2'). VISIONOS 1.02 answered 96 of 96 /player calls and served 175 of 178 opens, at a median 199 ms. Racing would double /player traffic, with the bot-flag risk the paper cites, for no measured gain. A single late hedge (PP-07) covers the tail.

Persisted cipher configs or a player-JS disk cache (§11 row 11, C9), and PoToken minting (C10, §3.2.2). The primary tier needs neither: 0 of 178 URLs carried n= or pot=. yt-dlp served 1 of 178 opens and the muxed tier 2, which does not justify the machinery.
BitChord's fixed 8 s next-track prefetch delay (D7). A typical song is fully downloaded ~0.75 s after it starts (6.0 MB/s), so PP-02 starts the next fill when the current one completes.

BitChord's 20-minute URL TTL that ignores expire= (§3.2.5). Step 2 measured 46 link-cache hits and 0 refusals of cached links. Keep expire minus 10 min (5 h cap) for links that have served bytes, and use 20 min only for links that have not (PP-09). Revisit if cached links start being refused after IP changes.

BitChord's opening-protecting evictor as specified (4 MB spans, 96 MB budget; §11 row 13). Our entries are whole 3-6 MB files, so whole-entry LRU with the current and next entries pinned gives the same protection. Revisit if partial long-track entries come to dominate the store.

Many connections per host (§11 row 16: 16 per host). Qt's network manager already opens up to 6 per host, playback and prefetch mostly go to different rr*.googlevideo.com hosts, and no queueing was observed.
NewPipe fast paths (§11 row 15). Monolist has no NewPipe; its nearest analogue, the yt-dlp tier, is a rare fallback.

Mid-song upgrade with a pre-buffered audition (C14, §4.6, §11 row 14). It belongs with the JioSaavn race already being built on branch 'jiosaavn', which uses a 1.2 s grace window instead, so it is not re-planned here. Once PP-01 exists, an audition is simply a broker fill of the upgrade's entry past the playhead.

A wake lock for network playback (C35, D12). With whole songs fetched in about a second and the next one prefetched (PP-02), a system sleep cannot starve playback of bytes. Whether Windows' audio stream already keeps the system awake is unverified (powercfg needs admin), so measure that before adding a power request.

items.title: Loudness normalisation from YouTube's per-format loudnessDb, with ReplayGain tags honoured, applied per file
items.change: Read the chosen format's own `loudnessDb` in InnerTube::player and carry it with the link. Also keep it per videoId in SQLite so replays, downloads, yt-dlp-tier links and JioSaavn's matched copy use it too. Pass it to mpv as a per-file `replaygain-fallback` of clamp(-loudnessDb, -15, 0) dB, via loadfile's options argument. Keep `replaygain=track` so tagged files use their tags; add `replaygain-preamp=+4` so RG2-tagged files hit the same -14 LUFS target, and `replaygain-clip=yes`. MEASURED (this plan's /player probe, 13 tracks, VISIONOS as the app sends it): top-level `audioConfig.loudnessDb` is missing on 13 of 13, `enablePerFormatLoudness` is true, and each format carries `loudnessDb`. `perceptualLoudnessDb` equals loudnessDb - 14 on all 13, so YouTube's reference is -14 LUFS. Read the per-format value first, and use perceptualLoudnessDb + 14 when it is missing. By default the gain only attenuates, which is YouTube's own rule. Add a Settings > Playback toggle, 'Even out loudness' (the Lumen design's 'Normalize volume', default on; Design/Lumen (HTML prototype)/app/settings.jsx:177). Follow-ups, only if measured worthwhile: (a) an optional +3 dB boost for quiet tracks, which needs a lavfi `alimiter` (present in the DLL) because mpv's gain has no limiter; (b) measuring the rendition that actually plays with lavfi `ebur128` read via `af-metadata`, for JioSaavn or download copies whose master may differ. Close-port alternative: none, since the reference JS (Appendix D.1) has no loudness or DSP module. Written from the §7.3 spec.

items.title: Gapless playback: keep the queue's next track appended in mpv's playlist (prefetch-playlist + gapless-audio)
items.change: Stop treating every boundary as stop() plus `loadfile replace`. Once the next queue item's link (or local path) is known, append it right after the current entry with `loadfile <url> insert-next -1 <options>`, using mpv_command_node with an options map. Set `prefetch-playlist=yes` and `gapless-audio=yes` (safe in shared mode, where the AO always opens at the 48 kHz mix rate: 43 of 43 inits). mpv then opens and reads the next file while the current one plays, and crosses the seam with no AO re-init. The controller adopts START_FILE of the appended entry as 'track advanced': split beginTrack into bookkeeping (closePlayEvent, listen, UI) and starting audio, and run only the bookkeeping. Next becomes `playlist-next` when the appended entry is the queue's next track. Every other action (Previous, pick, edit) keeps today's replace path, which clears the playlist, then re-appends. Queue edits and shuffle already call prefetchUpcoming, which swaps the appended entry (playlist-remove, then insert-next). Move user-agent, http-header-fields, start and audio-files from global options to per-file options, or an appended file inherits the current file's resume position and headers. Keep the whole ladder: an error END_FILE on the appended entry goes through the existing loadFailed rescue for that track. Also add the missing truncation check: an EOF more than 5 s before the duration on a network file is treated as an error and resumed. Close-port alternative: none (no gapless code in the reference JS; BitChord relies on Media3's playlist). Written from the §8.1 spec.

items.title: A 403 rescue should not pin 96 kbps AAC to the song for hours
items.change: After mpv refuses an InnerTube link, the muxed tier (itag 18, about 96 kbps AAC at 44.1 kHz) plays the rest of the song. Store rescue links under their own tier, and let resolve() from the InnerTube tier treat a muxed or yt-dlp rescue entry as a miss. The next play then asks InnerTube again (199 ms median) for Opus 251, and the ladder stays intact if that link is refused again. Coordinate with the cache planner's C3 row: this is the link-level half of one entry per rendition. Close-port alternative: resolve.js StreamChoice/cache keys by quality (App. D.3 'URL cache keyed by quality'), but it is simpler written directly.

items.title: Optional equal-power crossfade with a second mpv handle (off by default; gapless stays the default)
items.change: Add a standby MpvEngine. About 4 s before the fade, load the next track into it (its link is normally already cached: 22 of 22 skips were link-cache hits in Step 2) at volume-gain -96 dB, paused and pre-filled. At fade start, unpause it and ramp both handles' `volume-gain` along sin/cos in dB on a 30 ms timer, with progress read from the incoming handle's time-pos, so a pause freezes the blend. Then move current-track bookkeeping, UI, listen and lyrics to the incoming handle and stop the outgoing one. Each file keeps its own per-file normalisation gain (QT1). Rules: no crossfade when the next item is the next track of the same album (use gapless instead), when either track is under 45 s, when the fade exceeds half a track, or in video mode. If the standby is not ready within 12 s, fall back to the gapless or replace path with a 120 ms ramp. A skip during a fade completes it at once. Setting: a 0-12 s slider (the Lumen design's control, settings.jsx:161-172). Recommend default 0 (off), where Lumen had 4 s, because crossfading album segues is destructive; the owner decides. lavfi `afade` with curve=qsin (present in the DLL) is an alternative ramp to evaluate for sample accuracy. Close-port alternative: none in the reference JS; BitChord's CrossfadeController is GPL Kotlin and Automix is AGPL (Orchard). Written from the §8.1 spec.

items.title: Mid-song upgrade to JioSaavn's late 320 kbps answer (C14): first at user-made discontinuities, audition-plus-crossfade only if measured worthwhile
items.change: On the jiosaavn branch, a JioSaavn match that misses the 1.2 s grace is 'kept for the next time'. Variant A (build first): when that late match arrives for the song now playing, mark it ready. At the next discontinuity the listener causes anyway (a seek, a resume after a pause of 10 s or more, or a repeat-one loop), reload from JioSaavn at the target position through the existing load(startAt) path. Swap only if at least 20 s remain, the JioSaavn kbps exceeds YouTube's by at least 96, and the new duration agrees within 3 s. A refusal calls refuseSaavn and resumes on YouTube at the same second, so the ladder is untouched. The videoId's loudness gain (QT1) applies to both renditions. Variant B (M, needs QT6's standby handle): audition JioSaavn silently in the standby handle, pre-filled 12 s past the playhead, then make a 550 ms equal-power swap. Allow it only when the two durations differ by 0.3 s or less; otherwise wait for a discontinuity. Build B only if the branch's logs show 'did not answer within 1200 ms' on a meaningful share of first plays. prefetchTrack already asks JioSaavn for the next queued song, so in continuous listening the verdict is usually known before the song starts. Close-port alternative: reference sources/resolve.js (`worthSwapping`, `sameRecordingAs`, `upgradeFor`), a close port of §4.6's rules, which is GPL-3.0. Write our own from §4.6; the thresholds are facts we may reuse.

rejected: Changing how 44.1 kHz AAC is resampled (soxr, a larger audio-resample-filter-size, forcing audio-samplerate): in shared mode the AO always opens at the 48 kHz mix rate (43 of 43 inits), so the in-app float swresample replaces the Windows mixer's resampling rather than adding to it, and soxr (present in the DLL) would not be audibly better. The real fix is not picking 44.1 kHz when Opus exists (QT4: 1 of 13 probed tracks). The rest ('Last Last', which offers no Opus, and JioSaavn's AAC) are resampled once, in float, which is fine. Revisit only inside QT8's exclusive mode, where the device follows the source rate.

Automix / beat-matched transitions (C30, §8.2-8.4): the code is ported from AGPL Orchard plus ONNX models, costs about 7 s of analysis per track, carries defects A1-A5 and A7, and needs QT6 first. No measured listener need on this desktop player.
Porting BitChord's PrecisionAudioSink float DSP path (§7.1): mpv's filter chain is already float end to end (C23 ✅; 43 of 43 outputs float), so there is nothing to fix.
Forcing 16-bit output or copying BitChord's PCM_16 default (Q1): ours is float by default, and the paper counts BitChord's default as a defect.
Standalone dither (C25/Q4): no effect while nothing is re-quantised in-app (43 of 43 float outputs). It is only added inside QT8, for integer exclusive output.

A platform-effect or global normaliser (BitChord's shared LoudnessEnhancer, or lavfi loudnorm/dynaudnorm always on): it changes dynamics, costs CPU on every sample, and switches gain at the wrong moment (A6). QT1 uses a static per-file gain from YouTube's own measurement instead.

A positive loudness boost without a limiter (copying BitChord's +3 dB cap verbatim): LoudnessEnhancer limits, but mpv's gain does not, so +3 dB on a quiet dynamic master clips at high volume. It stays an optional QT1 follow-up behind lavfi alimiter; attenuate-only already cuts the probed spread from 12.45 to 4.68 dB.
DRC filtering as a separate project (Q7): 0 of 13 probed VISIONOS responses carried a DRC format, so it is only a one-line guard in QT4.
Crossfade with lavfi acrossfade inside one mpv: acrossfade needs two inputs in one filter graph, and mpv plays playlist entries one after another, so a second handle (QT6) is the way.

The version-swap aligner for the first C14 cut (§8.5, cross-correlation of RMS envelopes): not justified until the share of late JioSaavn answers is measured. QT7 variant A hides any offset inside a user seek.
Samsung FLAC / vendor codec blacklist (§6.1, C27) and container self-healing (§6.2, C31): N/A or already covered, since libmpv pins FFmpeg's own decoders and detects the container from the bytes.

An EQ, spatializer and silence skipping (§7.2, §7.5): not in this area's priorities and not engine speed or quality issues. ROADMAP.md:305 already lists EQ/speed as unassessed app work (lavfi equalizer via af-command if wanted later). A spatializer would need to avoid Q9.

items.title: Provider framework: parallel start, ordered harvest, instant winner, cancellable losers, per-provider cache, confidence gate
items.change:
Replace the serial chain with a LyricsProvider interface and a race coordinator:
- Start every enabled provider at once. Lazy ones start only if nothing is found.
- Harvest in the user's priority order, with a 6 s wall-clock deadline per provider.
- Show the first gated timed answer at once. After a 1.2 s patience window (the same grace the JioSaavn race uses), show the best answer in hand instead.
- Upgrade in place to a higher-ranked word-synced answer only while the pane is hidden or before the first sung line.
- Keep line-synced and plain fallbacks in separate slots.
- Abort losers with QNetworkReply::abort() or InnerTube Slot release.
- Cache each provider's outcome in a lyrics_results table keyed (videoId, provider). Errors stay in memory only.
The coordinator uses one shared QNetworkAccessManager and a generation counter. Every answer passes LY-3's gate: title plus artist, or the videoId, plus duration within 3 s for timed and 10 s for plain. Leading and trailing credit lines are stripped from bounded windows.

PaxSenix's keyless Apple route (§10.1 #4): it scrapes Apple Music's web-player developer JWT out of Apple's JavaScript and calls amp-api.music.apple.com with it, which is a token extracted from another app. It also failed silently until restart once the token expired (L16). BiniLyrics, BetterLyrics and LyricsPlus (LY-7) serve the same Apple TTML without us touching Apple's token.

Other providers in the same class, not in BitChord but common in other players: Spotify's internal lyrics API (needs the user's sp_dc cookie plus a TOTP secret lifted from Spotify's web player), KuGou's KRC word timing (XOR key embedded in the KuGou client) and NetEase's eapi/weapi (keys embedded in its clients). Left out for the same reasons. BitChord itself never requests KRC (§10.5).

The blocking ISRC identify step before the race (§10.3). It adds 2.5 s nominal and up to 6 s in practice (L2), we have no ISRC source today (C16: 'isrc' occurs nowhere in src/), and BiniLyrics matches server-side on title, artist, album and duration anyway. Pass an ISRC only when one is already known, such as a local file's tags (L10).
Waiting for every provider to finish before publishing (L1), and racing all six LyricsPlus mirrors on every lookup (L7).

Re-running the whole race on every play with no result cache (§10.4 step 9). Our SQLite cache answers in 28 ms median (n=86) and is one of the four scorecard rows where we lead (C43). It is kept and extended per provider instead.
Separate lookups for the UI, the media session and downloads (L4). We keep one store and one in-flight lookup per videoId (C48, another row where we lead).
YouTube captions at rank 10, where with default settings they beat LRCLIB and Musixmatch, keeping '[Music]' cues as lyrics (L17). Captions are kept only as the last, lazy timed provider (LY-11).

The 'Prioritize syllable sync' toggle, which holds line-synced answers while waiting for word timing and lets plain text outrank line sync (§10.2, L3). It is replaced by LY-5's 1.2 s patience window with in-place upgrade and separate line and plain slots.

Porting the paper's reference JavaScript or its 546 offline test fixtures (Appendix D.4, GPL-3.0). Monolist is MIT, so every item above is written from the paper as a specification, with our own fixtures. Endpoint names, parameters and field names are used as facts.

issues.problem: Rated L, but this is four projects plus a change of transport that Step 2 never measured. The four projects: a stream_cb reader, a sparse disk store with refresh, a SQLite index with LRU and a Clear UI, and a fake-googlevideo self-test. The transport change moves every googlevideo byte from mpv's libcurl to Qt's QNetworkAccessManager. This libmpv is a git build, mpv v0.41.0-1050 with -Dlibcurl=enabled (checked in libmpv-2.dll). QNAM uses HTTP/2 and Schannel by default. The pacing threshold (8-12 MiB), the UA result (5 URLs x 8 variants) and the one-shot-403 rate (2 of 8) were all measured through curl, not QNAM. So the gate 'first play must stay within ±10 ms of 553.5 ms' has no evidence behind it yet.
issues.suggestion: Split it into phases. (1) A spike: a monolist:// read-through with no disk, on a QNAM owned by the broker thread. Re-run bench_B 'seq' and bench_C_rangesize through it to re-measure open time, pacing and 403s. (2) Only if (1) passes the ±10 ms gate: whole-file entries up to 8 MiB. (3) Partial entries plus mid-file refresh. Rate it XL overall, or L per phase.

issues.problem: The ~20 s stall timeout before read_fn returns -1 means up to 20 s of silence before the loadFailed ladder runs. That is D10 (no liveness check) in a new place. A read_fn blocked while waiting on the fill also delays a user seek, because mpv's demuxer thread only acts on the seek after the read returns.
issues.suggestion: read_fn returns whatever bytes are available (partial reads) and never waits to fill the buffer. Add a no-bytes watchdog of about 5 s. It first reconnects to the same URL at the current offset, once. Next it refreshes the link, bypassing the link cache. If that fails it returns an error so the existing ladder runs. Keep 20 s only as an absolute cap. Add a case to --broker-test: the server stalls mid-body for 30 s, and audio must resume within 8 s.

issues.problem: 'Honour MONOLIST_DATA_DIR' points the store at the database's folder. AppDatabase uses AppDataLocation (src/appdatabase.cpp:21), which is the roaming profile on Windows, so up to 1 GiB would roam. The audio_cache index is planned inside the main database (appdatabase.cpp near 193). If the index keeps the bound URL, it writes the user's public IP (googlevideo URLs carry ip=) and expire= to disk, a data leak. macOS can purge ~/Library/Caches while the index still says an entry is complete, which is D1 again.
issues.suggestion: Keep the files and their index in QStandardPaths::CacheLocation, as ArtworkCache already does (src/artworkcache.cpp:185), with MONOLIST_DATA_DIR only as a test override. Persist only key, itag, clen, lmt and size; keep URLs and headers in memory. 'Complete' means file size == clen, checked at open with the same key function, never read from the index alone.

issues.problem: The pin (C4) will serve saavn:<id>:<kbps> bytes for a videoId with no further check. That is a wrong-song risk. The jiosaavn branch is still correcting its matcher (commit 855317d 'Stop JioSaavn playing a dub or another version'). A verdict also changes when JioSaavn or its India headers are switched off (setSaavnEnabled / setSaavnIndiaHeaders). A stale pin would keep playing the wrong recording from disk. The plan also never says whether a pinned entry skips the branch's race, which holds YouTube's answer for up to kSaavnGraceMs = 1200 ms (branch streamresolver.cpp:28).
issues.suggestion: Store each pin with the verdict's source, the matcher version and the JioSaavn settings in force, and invalidate it when any of them changes. A complete pinned entry plays without running the race. Test: pin a JioSaavn entry, flip its verdict to no-match, and check that YouTube's entry plays, not the cached JioSaavn bytes.

issues.problem: 'A mid-file 403 is re-resolved and continued at the same byte offset' would go through StreamResolver::resolve. That answers from m_cache first (src/streamresolver.cpp:109-115), so it hands back the very URL just refused. Separately, QT4 changes the format ranking, so a fresh /player could legitimately pick another itag, and the bytes would no longer continue the same file.
issues.suggestion: Give the broker refresh(videoId, itag): it invalidates the link, forces a new /player, and fails when the same itag+clen+lmt is not offered. On failure the ladder resumes by time into a new key. Make the QT4 ranking deterministic, so that a refresh reproduces the same choice.

issues.problem: PP-02 and QT2 both schedule next-track prefetch, and both claim the same measured rows. Natural-end gap (334 ms today): ~45-80 ms under PP-02, ~0-20 ms under QT2. Skip (412.5 ms today): 90-130 ms under PP-02, 100-150 ms under QT2. Both savings are the same ~247 ms HTTP open, so they do not add up. Two schedulers acting on one entry is also a D1 risk.
issues.suggestion: Give each part one owner. PP-02 fills the bytes. QT2, once PP-01 exists, appends the monolist:// entry of the same pinned key. Count the skip gain once, and credit QT2 only with the remaining ~40 ms plus the drain. Build order: PP-01, then PP-02, then QT2.

issues.problem: 'Prefetch the rendition that would actually play' conflicts with timing. The branch's prefetchTrack gets JioSaavn's answer asynchronously, so a fill started as soon as YouTube's link is known wastes 3-6 MB whenever JioSaavn wins, which is D1 in another form. Separately, 'fetch only the link for the row after that' calls StreamResolver::prefetch. That walks the whole ladder, including yt-dlp and muxed (src/streamresolver.cpp:256), so row+2 can start yt-dlp processes. The launch fill also competes with launch traffic: googlevideo ran at 4.9 MB/s at window-ready against 6.0 later.
issues.suggestion: Start the fill only once the next row's verdict is final: Match, NoMatch, or its grace window expired. Limit row+2 to the InnerTube tier. Start the launch fill after PP-03 lands and after Home has loaded. Log wasted bytes per verdict. If QNetworkInformation reports no Metered feature on macOS, treat the connection as unmetered.

issues.problem: 'The other five objects lose nothing' is not verified. Each InnerTube object has its own QNAM (src/innertube.cpp:696), and its home-page GET (718-721) fills that QNAM's jar with .youtube.com cookies (VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE, YSC). Those cookies then go out with the music.youtube.com calls from Catalog, Search, Recommender and Lyrics. ROADMAP.md:249 already expects Home's continuation to need that visitor cookie. After the change, the stream side would also send a persisted visitorData on the next launch with no matching cookie in its jar.
issues.suggestion: Share one QNetworkCookieJar across the six QNAMs (setCookieJar, then setParent(nullptr) on the jar), or have the holder seed the cookie. A/B test browse, search and next with and without the cookie, and /player with the id but no cookie. Keep the EU-consent case (ROADMAP.md:303) in scope. Effort S -> M.

issues.problem: 'Write closePlayEvent's UPDATE after stop()/load' means, for a stream, waiting until the next track resolves. A failed resolve or a quit in between loses the listened duration, which the code says exists only at that moment (playbackcontroller.cpp:929-931). The size of the gain also depends on history size: resolved-to-loadfile is 14 ms median (20 p90) at launch (step2_result.json) but 54.5-78.5 ms in a warm session. Part of the cost is duplicated: playRecorded triggers Library::reloadHistory, whose historyChanged runs Catalog::reloadRecent a second time (main.cpp:253-255).
issues.suggestion: Capture position and ids synchronously, then do the write in a QTimer::singleShot(0) right after stop(). Collapse the double reloadRecent into one. Measure on a database with a realistic history size, not the scratch one.

issues.problem: PP-05's second half and QT3 are the same change (keep rescue links out of the main slot), with conflicting lifetimes: 'this play only' against '20 min'. Neither tests the likeliest real trigger of the 'serves one request, then 403' mode. A seek beyond the buffered span of a paced long track (2.1 s buffered after 1 s of play) makes mpv send a second request. On 2 of 8 fresh long-track URLs that request is refused. Today that probably ends in either an itag-18 rescue (3.4-5.4 s) or a silent EOF that calls next().
issues.suggestion: Merge QT3 into PP-05 and keep 'this play only'. Add a test: --play on the 13:32 track with --at 600, over 8 or more fresh resolves. Log whether each seek ends in a 403 rescue, an EOF skip, or a clean seek.

issues.problem: The EOF-before-duration check appears in both PP-06 and QT2. Resetting m_consecutiveFailures 'when audio actually starts' needs a signal that main does not have; only the bench instrumentation logs FILE_LOADED and PLAYBACK_RESTART. Comparing against the queue row's durationMs (YouTube Music metadata) instead of the file's own duration would produce false positives on tracks with intros.
issues.suggestion: Keep the check only in PP-06 and compare against MpvEngine's duration (m_duration). Add PLAYBACK_RESTART, or the first time-pos > 0, as the 'started' signal. Effort S -> S/M.

issues.problem: Four problems. (1) 'None for prefetch' changes current behaviour. Today prefetch falls through to yt-dlp when InnerTube fails (streamresolver.cpp:256), so the rule moves a 2.9 s resolve into the skip itself. (2) Downloads already run up to 3 yt-dlp processes at once (downloadmanager.h:164), which is exactly the §3.2.4 concurrency-collapse case under x64 emulation. (3) Qt 6 uses HTTP/2 by default, so a hedged /player sent 'on a fresh connection' through the same QNAM is multiplexed onto the stalled connection. The existing 1.2 s retry (innertube.cpp:919-933) has the same flaw. (4) The non-blocking cancel fixes only the Windows job wait; the Unix branch still blocks in waitForFinished(1000) (ytdlp.cpp:110), which matters for macOS.
issues.suggestion: Run yt-dlp one process at a time: a foreground resolve pre-empts prefetch and pauses download extraction. Keep prefetch's yt-dlp rung rather than banning it. Send the hedge through a second QNAM, or with Http2AllowedAttribute=false on its own pool. Fix both platform branches of stopProcess.

issues.problem: The interim (a per-file curl-max-request-size in mpvengine.cpp) brings in the 'one request, then 403' mode (2 of 8 fresh long-track URLs) for no audible gain: 0 stalls in 1,555 s. The option exists only because this libmpv is a 2026 git build with the curl stream compiled in. A macOS libmpv (ROADMAP M06) may fetch through FFmpeg's http instead, where the equivalent is stream-lavf-o request_size; the embedded ytdl_hook sets both.
issues.suggestion: Drop the interim and chunk only inside the broker, where a refresh is transparent. Before building, measure how many plays it would help: the share of recent/history rows with duration_ms above ~7.5 min (about 8 MiB of Opus 251). If a stop-gap is ever needed, set both options and land PP-06 first.

issues.problem: A 10-minute 'unplayable' verdict keyed only by videoId would skip region-blocked songs that the jiosaavn race could serve. The India headers exist for exactly that catalogue. Letting a cancelled job's late /player answer fill the cache can also overwrite a newer link or a rescue entry.
issues.suggestion: Key verdicts per source, and skip a song only when every enabled source has a verdict. Fill from a late answer only when no newer entry exists for that key.

issues.problem: Under default settings the reuse path would almost never run. skipNonMusic defaults to true (downloadmanager.h:175; ytdlp.cpp:618 adds --sponsorblock-remove music_offtopic), and that step needs yt-dlp's segment data. The benefit is also unmeasured.
issues.suggestion: Defer it until PP-01 is proven. If kept, gate it on skipNonMusic=false and on the cached itag matching the chosen format, and rate the impact very low.

issues.problem: There are three separate sign-in slots (PP-11, QT9 and LY-15's SLOT) plus PP-03's holder hook, all for one pending decision. The rejected list also dismisses cipher/player-JS caching and PoToken (C9, C10) because VISIONOS needs neither. But signed-in streaming through www.youtube.com most likely means WEB or WEB_REMIX clients, which need both (§3.2.1 table: WEB_REMIX cipher + PoToken).
issues.suggestion: Make one [SIGN-IN SLOT], with sub-bullets for streaming, formats and loudness, visitorData, and lyrics. Mark the C9/C10 rejections 'revisit if the research needs a web client'. The gate: signed-out benchmark medians unchanged.

issues.problem: Rated high, but the drop in spread from 12.45 to 4.68 dB is derived from YouTube's own loudnessDb for 13 probed tracks. Step 2 lists loudness spread as not measured (scorecard line 111), and loudness is not in the owner's §11 priorities. Default-on also plays the median track ~5 dB quieter for every user.
issues.suggestion: Label the impact 'estimated' until the ebur128 cross-check has run, and schedule QT1 after the §11 speed items. Put the default-on question and a new volume default to the owner as one decision.

issues.problem: Three gaps. (1) mpv's manual calls prefetch-playlist experimental, with no guarantee that it is safe. (2) The early open happens while the current file's options are still active, so the appended entry's per-file user-agent and http-header-fields may not reach it (to be verified on this build). That matters for muxed/yt-dlp rescue links, which need their headers (playbackcontroller.cpp:1054-1056). (3) 'The AO always opens at 48 kHz' holds for WASAPI shared mode (43/43 Windows inits). On CoreAudio, gapless-audio=yes keeps the first file's rate for the whole session. Also, loadfile's index argument and insert-next need mpv ≥ 0.38, and cmake/FindMpv.cmake enforces no minimum version.
issues.suggestion: Build QT2 after PP-01, so appended entries are monolist:// URLs whose headers live in the broker entry. Add a libmpv ≥ 0.38 check to FindMpv.cmake. Measure the AO format on a Mac before choosing gapless-audio=yes or weak per platform.

issues.problem: Passing codec and kbps into the JioSaavn race edits the unmerged branch (streamresolver.h:94-96). A new ranking also changes which itag gets cached and refreshed, which the PP-01 refresh check depends on.
issues.suggestion: Land the Opus-first rule and the DRC guard on main after the merge. Keep the selection deterministic, and log itag, codec and kbps with every resolve.

issues.problem: The 'Stream info' line overlaps ROADMAP P06, which is open. P06 already calls for a status line with a source label such as 'Streaming · InnerTube'.
issues.suggestion: Build QT5 as P06's engine half: one status line fed by the properties mpv confirms, not a second label.

issues.problem: QT7 plans C14 (mid-song upgrade and audition). The playback-path plan rejects the same item as belonging to the in-flight jiosaavn work, not to be re-planned. QT7's files are also line numbers on an unmerged branch.

issues.problem: In WASAPI exclusive mode, ao-volume drives the endpoint's master volume. The Monolist slider would change the device's system volume, and the change would persist after the app exits. On macOS the exclusive (hog) CoreAudio output may not support ao-volume at all. Effort M looks low given the device-busy fallback, per-device settings, and the QT2/QT6 interlocks.

issues.problem: The item covers the pin where LRCLIB errors and YouTube Music's plain answer sticks, but not the reverse. When LRCLIB misses cleanly and the YouTube Music leg errors, lyrics.cpp:340-347 stores 'none' for 3 days. That is also an L14 error-as-miss.

issues.problem: On a database miss, LRCLIB's /api/get may try external sources, which gives a slow tail the 30-track audit may not show. With LY-5 and LY-7, looking up at every track start plus the next row sends every played track and the next one to 6 or more third-party hosts. SimpMusic would receive our videoId. This happens even for users who never open lyrics.

Both edit src/lyrics.h:110 and the construction in main.cpp. The 1.2 s patience window is borrowed from the JioSaavn grace, with no lyrics measurement behind it (LRCLIB's leg median is 447 ms).

issues.problem: Rated high, but word timing is 0/30 with today's providers. Its value depends entirely on LY-7 delivering word-timed answers, and LY-7 has no hit-rate estimate. The same applies to LY-8.
issues.suggestion: Rate LY-6 and LY-8 as conditional, and build them only after LY-7's --lyrics-providers run shows a meaningful word-timed share.

issues.problem: Three problems. (1) It ranks six unmeasured community relays ahead of LRCLIB, which measured 28/28 line-synced with correct text on 27/28. (2) BetterLyrics, Portato and Unison all run on boidu.dev (§10.1 rows 2, 3, 9), so one operator gets three requests per track, doubled with prefetch; the breadth is smaller than it looks. (3) The rejected list refuses routes built on an Apple JWT or Spotify secrets, yet this item accepts relays that serve the same Apple TTML and QQ data from their servers, and LY-15 accepts PaxSenix's keyed Spotify and Musixmatch proxies.
issues.suggestion: Keep LRCLIB first until --lyrics-providers shows each new provider's correct-recording rate on the 30-track list and on a long-tail list. Word timing may upgrade an answer but never outrank LRCLIB by default. Treat boidu.dev as one rate-limit domain. Ask the owner to rule explicitly on the policy 'no secret in our binary, relays allowed'.

issues.problem: Rated M, but it holds five providers. KuGou is a two-step search and download. YouTube captions go through get_transcript with protobuf-encoded params (§10.1 row 10). There are two HTML scrapers. JioSaavn lyrics must be wired into the unmerged branch's match API.

**Range chunking.** The playback plan was right to demote it despite the owner listing it first under §11. It affects 1 of 12 benchmark tracks, and its pacing (36.8 kB/s, 1.85x real time) produced 0 stalls. The owner should hear that the measurements overturned the paper here.

- UA and per-client headers: no effect across 5 URLs x 8 variants.
- Racing two InnerTube clients: 96 of 96 /player calls succeeded.

- LY-6, LY-7 and LY-8 as 'high' are contingent: word timing is 0 of 30 with today's providers.

# Step 3: the engine plan, for your approval

**In short.** Step 2 showed that our first play of a new song is already level with BitChord: a median of 553.5 ms in a warm session. BitChord wins on what comes after that first play:
- replays: 421.5 ms for us, no network at all for BitChord;
- skips: 412.5 ms;
- the silence between songs: 334 ms;
- long tracks: 36.8 kB/s.

All four come from one missing piece: a disk cache of song bytes that sits in front of the resolver and is filled in advance with the next song. That cache tops the plan.

The launch delay is the cheapest big win, and it can be built now, before the JioSaavn merge. Today a play started the moment the window is ready waits a median 434.5 ms for visitorData.

For lyrics, the order is:
1. Stop storing a worse answer permanently.
2. Fix the search query.
3. Run the providers in parallel.
4. Add providers one at a time, each measured before it can rank above LRCLIB.

The YouTube ladder (InnerTube, then yt-dlp, muxed, Piped and Invidious) stays underneath every change. Each new layer has a switch that hands control back to the ladder.

**What the measurements overturned in the paper**
- **Range chunking (§11 row 1) is not a general speed-up for us.** googlevideo slows down only requests that ask for more than about 8-12 MiB.
  - Normal songs already arrive whole at 6.0 MB/s (n=93). 1 MiB ranges were slower on them (0.9-5.7 MB/s).
  - Only files over about 8 MiB (roughly 7.5 minutes or more of Opus) crawl, at 36.8 kB/s. Even those caused 0 stalls in 1,555 s of play.
  - So chunking is for long files only, and it goes inside the cache (rank 19).
- **The 500 ms start threshold (§11 row 5) is already beaten.** Audio starts a median 49 ms after the first bytes arrive (p90 209, n=176).
- **Matching the User-Agent or the per-client headers (§11 row 10) changed nothing** across 5 URLs x 8 variants.
- **A probe request before trusting a URL (§3.2.5) is not worth it.** It would add about 200 ms to every cold play in order to catch refusals on 1.1% of opens, and the first real read already catches every one of them.
- **Racing two InnerTube clients buys nothing we measured.** VISIONOS answered 96 of 96 /player calls. A second no-cipher client that is used only when VISIONOS fails is worth having (rank 9).

#### 1. PP-01: Byte cache in front of resolution (L, in three phases)
- **Change:** An AudioBroker thread serves mpv through a registered monolist:// protocol (mpv_stream_cb_add_ro). It reads from disk entries keyed `yt:<videoId>:<itag>:<clen>` (later `saavn:<id>:<kbps>`), and a miss fills the entry while the song plays.
  - Video, local files, downloads and manifests keep today's direct path.
  - A Settings switch restores direct googlevideo URLs.
- **Phase 1, spike (M):** Read-through with no disk, using a Qt network manager owned by the broker thread. Compare HTTP/1.1 with HTTP/2.
  - read_fn returns whatever bytes it has and never waits to fill the buffer.
  - After 5 s with no bytes, it reconnects once at the same offset, then refreshes the link (bypassing the link cache), then returns an error so today's ladder runs. 20 s is only an absolute cap.
  - Log the IP family of the /player connection and of the media connection.
  - **Gate:** a new song must start within ±10 ms of the post-merge baseline, with no new 403s and the same pacing as curl.
  - **If the gate fails:** try the same design behind a 127.0.0.1 server (random port, a per-session token in the path, identity URLs only, never an open proxy). If that fails too, stop, and build QT2 on plain URLs to get the skip and gap gains.
- **Phase 2 (L):** Whole-file entries up to 8 MiB.
  - Files and their index live in `QStandardPaths::CacheLocation`, as ArtworkCache already does (src/artworkcache.cpp:185). Not in the database's AppDataLocation (src/appdatabase.cpp:21), which roams on Windows.
  - Persist only key, itag, clen, lmt and size. URLs (they carry your IP and expire=) and headers stay in memory.
  - "Complete" means file size = clen, checked at open with the same key function.
  - 1 GiB cap, whole-entry LRU with the current and next songs protected, and a Clear action.
  - The pin records the JioSaavn verdict's source, the matcher version and the JioSaavn settings, and is dropped when any of them changes. A complete pinned entry plays without running the JioSaavn race.
- **Phase 3 (M):** Partial entries, plus a mid-file refresh through a new `refresh(videoId, itag)`. It forces a new /player call and fails unless the same itag, clen and lmt come back. PP-08 lives here.
